name: External Nose, Nasal Septum and Choanal Atresia

reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Septal haematoma: drain urgently or saddle nose follows
Bilateral choanal atresia: cyanosis relieved by crying in neonate
Kiesselbach plexus sits on anterior septum (Little area)
reference.pathophysiology: Cartilage survives on perichondrial blood flow, so haematoma or abscess separates and necroses it; embryonic buccopharyngeal membrane persistence plates the choana, while deviated growth between cartilage and bone bows the septum.
additionalDifferentials: Deviated septum versus turbinate hypertrophy on decongestion
Choanal atresia versus neonatal respiratory distress other causes
additionalInvestigations: Nasal endoscopy and septal examination after trauma
CT sinuses and choanae for atresia and surgical planning
ANCA and drug history for perforation workup
